---
title: "CSV Digital Event I/O"
---

## Overview

The CSV digital event loader reads `DigitalEventSeries` timestamps from CSV or TXT files.
Two batch modes are supported:

- **Identifier column**: One file with multiple columns; events are grouped by a label column.
- **Multi-file directory**: One timestamp file per series; files are loaded in alphabetical order
  and registered as `{name}_0`, `{name}_1`, … or `{name}_{file_stem}` when `append_filename` is true.

## File Location

```
src/IO/formats/CSV/digitaltimeseries/
├── Digital_Event_Series_CSV.hpp
└── Digital_Event_Series_CSV.cpp
```

## Option Structs

- `CSVEventLoaderOptions` — Single file; optional `identifier_column` for multi-series split.
- `CSVEventMultiFileLoaderOptions` — Directory of per-channel files (`.csv` / `.txt`).

## JSON Examples

### Multi-column CSV (identifier column)

```json
{
  "filepath": "spikes.csv",
  "data_type": "digital_event",
  "name": "spikes",
  "format": "csv",
  "scale": 30000,
  "identifier_column": 1,
  "clock": "master"
}
```

### Multi-file directory (one series per file)

```json
{
  "filepath": "spikes",
  "data_type": "digital_event",
  "name": "spikes",
  "format": "csv",
  "multi_file": true,
  "append_filename": true,
  "scale": 30000,
  "event_column": 0,
  "delimiter": "\t",
  "file_pattern": "*.txt",
  "clock": "master"
}
```

With `append_filename: true`, each series is registered as `{name}_{file_stem}` (e.g.
`spikes_23a` from `23a.txt`). Without it, series use numeric suffixes (`spikes_0`, …).

`filepath` must resolve to a directory when `multi_file` is true. Without `file_pattern`,
all `.csv` and `.txt` files in the directory are loaded. Files are sorted alphabetically by
filename before numbering suffixes.
